name: Electric Bike Sharing
description: Size the market for electric bike sharing in urban areas.
formula: SOM = Population x Penetration Rate x Purchase Frequency x Average Spend x Serviceable % x Obtainable Share %
solution_logic: Step 1: Identify addressable population = target_population x addressable_segment
Step 2: Apply penetration rate = addressable_population x penetration_rate
Step 3: Calculate annual spend per user = purchase_frequency x avg_spend_per_purchase
Step 4: Calculate TAM = penetrating_users x annual_spend_per_user
Step 5: Calculate SAM = TAM x serviceable_pct
Step 6: Calculate SOM = SAM x obtainable_share_pct
key_insight: This is a SOM question, not a TAM question -- obtainable_share_pct exists precisely because a new entrant into micromobility is fighting existing operators for a slice, not capturing the whole serviceable market.
common_mistakes: Stopping at the serviceable market and forgetting to apply obtainable share against competitors
Using national population instead of the specific launch city's urban residents
Pricing per-ride spend as if it were an annual subscription instead of rides times price-per-ride
framework_soundbite: Urban residents, in the service zone, riding at this frequency, at this price -- then cut it down to what you can actually win from competitors.
business_contexts: a micromobility operator evaluating a new city launch
a city transit authority sizing demand for e-bike sharing
question_patterns: A micromobility operator is deciding whether to launch e-bike sharing in a new city and wants to size the annual ridership revenue it could realistically capture against existing competitors.

serviceable_pct.unit: % within the launch city's service zone

prompts.advanced: A city transit authority is considering subsidizing an e-bike sharing operator whose ridership projections rely on adoption assumptions borrowed from a much denser peer city. Build an independent serviceable-obtainable-market estimate before the subsidy is approved.
prompts.beginner: Estimate the serviceable obtainable market for electric bike sharing rides in a major city, accounting for realistic competitive capture.
prompts.intermediate: A micromobility operator is deciding whether to launch e-bike sharing in a new city and wants to size the annual ridership revenue it could realistically capture against existing competitors.

approach_guidance.top_down_why: Start from urban residents, narrow to the service zone, apply penetration, then multiply by rides per year and price per ride -- narrowing down from the city's population.
approach_guidance.bottom_up_why: Or start from one rider: their annual spend (rides/year x price/ride), then scale up by penetrating riders and obtainable share against competitors. The more natural default for a usage-based business -- you're building from one rider's behavior, not a city population.
